Subject: Recap: parallel connection guardrails & requested rate quota

Hi Liam —

Great to speak earlier. Quick post-call recap and next steps so we have a single source of truth. I’ve attached the traffic profile you shared and our call diagram.

Key items we heard from your side:
- Workload: mixed streaming + sync generation for OCR and conversational flows (approx 30% streaming).
- Peak concurrency: 140 sustained concurrent active requests during end-of-day batch window; bursts up to ~420 for ~90s during marketing spikes.
- Typical request size: median ~350 tokens, 95th ~1,200 tokens for large OCR payloads.
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms for non-streaming; streaming per-token latency goal < 35ms.
- Connection constraints: frontend LB supports ~200 persistent upstream sockets per region; client side can multiplex but not beyond 250 long-lived connections.

Open clarifying questions (please confirm):
1) Is the 420 burst an absolute peak (single-minute) or repeated several times during the hour?
2) Do you expect multiple independent consumer clusters (multi-tenant) or a single logical pool hitting our endpoints?
3) Procurement contact and PO timeline (if moving to pilot).

Proposed immediate next steps from Redwood:
- We’ll propose an initial quota that covers sustained concurrency + 2x burst cushion and a connection-pooling recommendation that fits your LB constraints.
- Canaries: 2-week pilot, ramping from 10% → 50% → 100% traffic.
- Provide SOC2 evidence + sample DPA for legal review.

Action items:
- Liam: confirm answers to the 3 questions above and attach any additional traffic logs (if available) — due EOD Thu (8/6).
- Redwood (Sofia): draft quota proposal and pilot runbook — due Fri (8/6) morning.

Attachments: orchidpay-traffic-profile.csv, architectural-diagram.png

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Recap: parallel connection guardrails & requested rate quota

Sofia —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments. Quick answers:
1) The ~420 spike is normally a sharp marketing-triggered burst that lasts 60–120s and repeats 2–3 times during the busiest hour (not sustained across the hour).
2) Single logical pool (we’re a single-tenant workload per account) but we have two frontend clusters in us-west/us-east that split traffic ~70/30. Both will hit your hosted endpoints.
3) Procurement: salesops@orchidpay.com (CC'd). We can sign a pilot PO this month; enterprise legal will review the DPA but typically moves within 7–10 business days.

I attached our end-of-month QPS export (orchidpay-qps-report.pdf) — it includes per-minute spikes for July.

One more thing: our infra team is sensitive to long-lived connection counts; they asked if Redwood can support connection pooling with connection reuse and a soft cap per IP to avoid exhausting the LB. If we can keep persistent sockets per region under ~220 that would be ideal.

Liam

OrchidPay

Thanks Liam — that helps a lot. Based on the profile and your LB constraint, here’s an initial Redwood proposal for the pilot. This is what we can provision quickly for a 2-week canary and then tune after live telemetry: 

Redwood pilot quota (proposed):
- Sustained concurrency reservation: 200 concurrent request slots (covers median + buffer).
- Burst allowance: 900 RPS for up to 2 minutes (to absorb the ~420 spikes across clusters).
- Connection pool guidance: 200–220 persistent upstream sockets per region with aggressive connection reuse/Keep-Alive (we’ll recommend client-side HTTP/2 multiplexing).
- Per-second rate limit (API key): 600 RPS sustained, with 900 RPS burst window as above.
- Token-based billable estimate: estimate ~18M tokens/month at current traffic — will produce an itemized projection for procurement.
- SLOs: p95 non-streaming latency <= 250ms; streaming per-token latency target <= 35ms; we’ll instrument prefix/KV caching for OCR payloads to reduce cost and latency.

Pilot runbook highlights:
- Week 0: config + onboarding, mutual smoke tests (10% traffic).
- Week 1: ramp to 50% with daily check-ins and telemetry review.
- Week 2: full cutover in pilot, then prepare production qty if things are green.

Ask: confirm you’re OK with the 200–220 connection cap per region as a hard limit from your side so we don’t exceed LB capacity. If you require 180 instead, we’ll recalculate the burst allowance needed.

I’ve linked the HubSpot deal and attached a short cost projection; Ben will follow up with a tailored ratecard and any pilot-discount details.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/OP-4382
